newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 21.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.

- Celebrations mark 50th annivesary of founding of Inner Mongolia Autonomous region. Vice Premier Zou Jiahua praises region as model in consolidating and developing unity among all ethnic nationalities.

- Shanghai residents participate in government campaign to build civilised environment, following "Seven Nos" -- no spitting, no littering, no smoking in public places, no rude language, no destroying of greenery or public properties and no crossing streets ignoring traffic lights.
- Sichuan provincial government removes four senior officials in steel company posts after mismanagement caused 300 million yuan in losses in first six months of this year.
- China becomes second largest market for Mastercard
- Sales and pre-tax profits of large enterprises and groups will account for 60-70 percent of major industries in five to 10 years
- Vice President of China Finance Institute Liu Hongru calls for improving quality of B share companies
- About 57.09 percent of foreign investment in Shanghai goes to industry in first half, and 17.45 percent to real estate
- Excessive construction of development zones, unscientific urban planning and reckless expansion of small towns cause appalling waste of land.
- China will expand length of express highways to 6,500 km by end of this century.

- After years of persistent losses and a sharp decrease in passengers, China's railway industry shows signs of revival. Profits growth has steadily edged up. accompanied by increase in traveller rates.
- Return of Hong Kong to China lures more property developers and investors to Shanghai.
- China's electronics industry chalks up a 20.9 percent increase in production in the first half of this year.
